chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the grave of Fatimah (peace be upon her), so he said: 'She was buried in her house, and when the Banu Umayya expanded the mosque, it became part of the mosque.'
ai.seo_question: Where was Fatimah (peace be upon her) originally buried and how did the mosque expansion affect her grave's location?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the historical location of Fatimah al-Zahra’s (AS) grave, confirming it was originally within her private residence before the Umayyad expansion of Masjid al-Nabawi incorporated it into the mosque's boundaries. This detail is significant in Shia scholarship for understanding the sanctity of her resting place and its integration into the Prophet’s mosque, distinguishing it from other burial sites. The hadith underscores the continuity of sacred space in Islamic tradition, linking the domestic sphere of the Prophet’s family with the communal worship space.
